Ran `consolidate` (read-only — it only surfaces candidates, doesn't change anything) across all spaces, then cross-checked the flagged pairs against the full claim set. Here's what's actually there, filtering out the noise `consolidate` also returned (a lot of its "contradictions" are just topically-adjacent facts that happen to embed similarly, not real conflicts — e.g. "container image is distroless" vs "images pushed to GHCR" aren't in tension, they're just both about images).

**One real thing to flag before handover — an actual contradiction:**
- "Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically." (id `...A7FY5`)
- "Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs `bin/ship.sh --staging` by hand." (id `...DJR7P`)

These directly disagree on how staging deploys work. Whoever inherits this needs the real answer before they merge anything.

**True duplicates (safe to merge, no conflict — just restated):**
- Test runner: "Tests in atlas are run through `cargo nextest run`; plain `cargo test` is not used." / "The atlas test suite is run with `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`." — same claim twice.
- Deploy command (3-way): "To ship atlas you run `bin/ship.sh`..." / "Project atlas is deployed by running `bin/ship.sh` from the repository root." / "Deploying atlas means executing `bin/ship.sh`; the old `make deploy` target is gone." — same fact, the third has one extra detail (old `make deploy` retired) worth keeping when merged.

**Genuinely ambiguous, not a clean duplicate — worth a human decision:**
- "Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more." vs "Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass." These read like two different mechanisms both called "feature flags" (a runtime env-var map vs. Cargo compile-time features). Left as-is, the next person won't know which one governs a given flag.

**Stale, past their shelf life (already flagged by the system as idle ~40 days, decaying):**
- "The branch under review is `spike/consolidate`." — a snapshot of in-progress work, no longer current.
- "The flaky test being chased this week is `pagination_ordering` in atlas-api." — a "this week" claim that's now old.

**One thing worth naming explicitly:** every atlas claim I found — all 117 — was written in a single burst on 2026-09-04 by the same session/writer (`desc-eval`), not accumulated across real work over time. That's consistent with this being seeded/fixture data rather than organic project memory. Worth confirming with whoever set this up before treating it as ground truth for the handover.

Nothing has been changed. Want me to (a) merge the two true-duplicate groups, (b) resolve or just surface the staging-deploy contradiction for someone to answer, and (c) drop the two stale entries?
